process_area.title: Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement

value_stream.name: Investor Relations, Capital Markets & Securities Disclosure

fields.Participants: CFO/CEO, Strategy (VS-33), Treasury (VS-18), R2R (VS-17), Governance (VS-36), Marketing/Comms (VS-14), ESG (VS-25), Legal (VS-100)
fields.Trigger: Program launch; annual IR plan; capital-markets event; strategic-plan refresh (VS-33); transaction (VS-130)
fields.Volume: 1 IR program across the 5 entities × investor/analyst/credit/lender audiences

workflows.name: IR Program Strategy, Investor Audience & Equity-Story / Capital-Markets Narrative Design

Automation Opportunity: - Narrative/drafting templates tied to FP&A actuals; IR KPI dashboards; audience-segmentation analytics
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749: narrative board/leadership-approved; forward statements disclosure-controlled (W5017); messaging reconciled to accounts/strategy
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-17/VS-17.4 (accounts/FP&A), VS-18/VS-170 (capital structure), VS-36 (governance), VS-100 (legal), W5010 (database), W5014 (website), W5017 (disclosure controls), W5018 (annual report)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Narrative-drift risk**: Investor messaging diverging from strategy/internal data → credibility loss; mitigated by strategy alignment & approval
- **Forward-statement risk**: Guidance/projections without disclosure-control backing → securities-law exposure (W5017); mitigated by disclosure-governance gate
- **Consistency risk**: Equity story conflicting with annual report/accounts (VS-17); mitigated by reconciliation
System Touchpoints: - IR/CRM platform; investor database (W5010); FP&A/strategy (VS-33/VS-17.4); treasury (VS-18); legal/disclosure (VS-100/W5017); IR website (W5014)
Time Estimate: - ~4–6 weeks annual IR plan; quarterly narrative refresh

steps.activity: Set the IR strategy & operating model: the investor/analyst/credit/lender audiences BuildRight engages, the equity story and capital-markets narrative (positioning, growth thesis, margin/cash-conversion story, multi-entity/intercompany clarity links VS-72), the disclosure posture (voluntary vs mandatory), the IR calendar (earnings, ASHM, ratings, events), and the IR KPIs (coverage, sentiment, valuation gap)

Build the equity-story & narrative materials: the core IR deck, fact book, segment/financial summaries, capital-structure and liquidity narrative (links VS-18/VS-170), and the consistency check vs the strategic plan (VS-33), annual report (W5018), and management accounts (VS-17)

Govern & align: leadership/board sign-off on the narrative and forward statements (links VS-36 governance), alignment of investor messaging with internal strategy, and the disclosure-controls linkage (W5017) so every external statement traces to approved, disclosed information

fields.Trigger: Continuous ownership tracking; capital-markets event; targeting campaign; transaction (VS-130)
fields.Volume: ~50–100 contacts in the investor/analyst/lender universe × ownership-change events

workflows.name: Investor & Shareholder Database, Targeting & Ownership Intelligence

Automation Opportunity: - Broker-survey/transfer-agent feed automation; ownership-threshold alerting; investor-CRM targeting
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749 (ownership tracked & threshold-monitored; privacy-compliant (VS-91); fair-disclosure enforced (W5017))
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury), VS-91 (privacy), VS-100/VS-22 (compliance), W5025/W5026 (transfer/ledger), W5023 (beneficial-ownership), W5032 (activist), W5009 (plan), W5015 (outreach)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Ownership-blindness risk**: Unknown beneficial owners / activist accumulation → surprise (links W5032); mitigated by ownership intelligence
- **Data-privacy risk**: Investor personal data (RA 10173); mitigated by privacy controls (VS-91)
- **Selective-disclosure risk**: Targeting one investor with material non-public info (W5017); mitigated by fair-disclosure protocol
System Touchpoints: - IR/CRM & investor database; transfer-agent feed (W5025/W5026); beneficial-ownership/broker-survey data; legal/disclosure (VS-100/W5023); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Maintain the investor/shareholder & analyst database: registered and beneficial owners (from transfer agent W5025/W5026 and broker surveys), institutional/lender/analyst contacts, ownership concentration, and the targeting/segmentation by type (long-only, credit, ESG, retail)

Run ownership intelligence: track share-movements and concentration, beneficial-ownership analysis (links W5023 related-party/beneficial-ownership disclosure), street-name vs registered, and flag threshold crossings / activist accumulation (links W5032 activist response)
Target & prioritize outreach: prioritize investors/analysts by fit/value, plan outreach (W5015), and feed the IR plan (W5009) and event calendar (W5012)

fields.Participants: CFO/CEO, R2R (VS-17), FP&A (VS-17.4/VS-33), Treasury (VS-18), Legal (VS-100), ESG (VS-25)
fields.Trigger: Quarterly/annual close (VS-17); guidance cycle; investor calendar
fields.Volume: ~4 quarterly + 1 annual results cycle per year × audiences

workflows.name: Periodic Investor Communications — Earnings, Results & Guidance Management

Automation Opportunity: - Investor-deck generation from FP&A actuals; webcast/Q&A logging; consensus tracking; disclosure-checklist workflow
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749: results reconciled to closed books; forward statements disclosure-controlled (W5017); fair simultaneous release; script/legal-reviewed
Cross-references: - links to VS-17 (close/accounts), VS-17.4/VS-33 (FP&A/strategy), W5017 (disclosure controls), W5014 (website), W5013 (consensus), W5019 (ad-hoc disclosure), W5018 (annual report)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Disclosure-breach risk**: Releasing material info in earnings without fair disclosure (W5017); mitigated by simultaneous public release
- **Guidance-miss risk**: Guidance not met → credibility/litigation risk; mitigated by conservative, control-backed ranges
- **Numbers-mismatch risk**: Investor comms disagreeing with filed accounts (VS-17); mitigated by reconciliation & close tie-out
System Touchpoints: - R2R/close (VS-17); FP&A (VS-17.4); disclosure-controls (W5017); IR website/webcast (W5014); consensus (W5013); legal (VS-100)
Time Estimate: - ~3–5 days prep per quarterly cycle; ~half-day earnings engagement

steps.activity: Prepare results & earnings communications: the results press release, investor presentation, financial & segment commentary, MD&A-style narrative, and guidance/range — all reconciled to the closed books (VS-17) and reviewed through disclosure controls (W5017) before release
Conduct the results engagement: earnings call/webcast (Q&A prep, script, hot-topics), investor portal publication (W5014), and analyst follow-up — all on fair-disclosure basis (W5017)

Manage guidance & forward statements: set/affirm/withdraw guidance with disclosure-control sign-off (W5017), track consensus (W5013), and manage any guidance update/withdrawal as a disclosure event (W5019)

fields.Participants: CFO/CEO, Strategy (VS-33), Marketing/Comms (VS-14), Corporate Security (VS-159), Legal (VS-100)
fields.Trigger: IR calendar; capital-markets strategy; transaction (VS-130); rating review

workflows.name: Investor Events, Analyst Day, Roadshow & Conference Participation Management

Automation Opportunity: - Event/meeting CRM; feedback capture; sentiment analytics (W5029); approved-material distribution
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749: only disclosure-approved materials used (W5017); fair-disclosure enforced; principal security coordinated (VS-159); feedback captured
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-159/W4684 (security), VS-14 (comms), W5009 (narrative), W5010 (database), W5017 (disclosure), W5029 (sentiment), W5031 (ROI)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Selective-disclosure risk**: 1:1 meetings leaking material non-public info (W5017); mitigated by fair-disclosure protocol & approved materials only
- **Security risk**: Principal (CEO/CFO) appearance exposure (links VS-159); mitigated by security coordination
- **Message-drift risk**: Roadshow narrative diverging from approved equity story; mitigated by material control
Time Estimate: - ~2–4 weeks per major event (analyst day); ~roadshow week(s)

steps.activity: Plan the event/roadshow: objective (strategic-story refresh, rating support, transaction), audience/targeting (W5010), agenda, materials (reconciled to W5009 narrative & disclosure-controlled W5017), logistics, and corporate-security coordination for principal appearances (links VS-159/W4684)
Execute the event/roadshow: presentations, 1:1/1:few investor & analyst meetings (fair-disclosure basis W5017), conference participation, and Q&A tracking/log
Follow up & measure: capture investor feedback/sentiment (W5029), update the CRM/database (W5010), and assess event ROI/coverage impact (W5031)

fields.Trigger: Continuous relationship; rating-review cycle; earnings/guidance; transaction (VS-130)

workflows.name: Sell-Side Analyst, Credit-Rating-Agency & Consensus-Estimate Relationship Management

Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749 (fair-disclosure enforced (no selective correction); rating briefed proactively; consensus monitored; covenant linkage tracked (VS-18))
Cross-references: - links to VS-18/VS-170 (treasury/capital/covenant), W5011 (guidance), W5017 (disclosure), W5019 (ad-hoc disclosure), W5029 (analytics), VS-100 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Selective-correction risk**: Privately correcting one analyst's model (W5017/RA 8799); mitigated by fair-disclosure rule
- **Rating-action risk**: Unexpected downgrade raising borrowing cost / breaching covenants (links VS-18 W319); mitigated by proactive rating engagement
- **Consensus-divergence risk**: Consensus materially off guidance → volatility; mitigated by monitoring & disclosed updates (W5019)
System Touchpoints: - IR/CRM; consensus/estimate service; rating-agency platform; treasury/covenant (VS-18/VS-170); disclosure-controls (W5017); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Manage sell-side analyst relationships: analyst coverage development, fact-checking/correction of published models, Q&A on fair-disclosure basis (W5017), and tracking of estimates/consensus/range

Manage credit-rating-agency relationships: rating briefings, the management/credit presentation (financials, liquidity links VS-18, capital structure links VS-170, covenants), rating-action response, and tracking of the rating/outlook (which sets borrowing cost across facilities)
Manage consensus & guidance gap: monitor consensus vs guidance (W5011), flag material divergence, and decide any disclosure/guidance response (W5019) — never selectively correcting one analyst

fields.Trigger: Site launch; disclosure publication; continuous content refresh

workflows.name: Investor Relations Website, IR Portal & Digital Disclosure-Channel Management

Automation Opportunity: - SEC-filing→website auto-publish; disclosure archive; subscriber alerting; content-freshness alerts
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749: disclosures posted timely & publicly (fair disclosure W5017); content accurate/fresh; privacy/accessibility compliant; audit trail kept
Cross-references: - links to VS-27 (IT), VS-10 (digital), VS-91 (privacy), VS-88 (retention), VS-14 (brand), W5011 (webcast), W5017 (disclosure), W5018/W5019 (SEC filings), W5020 (ASHM materials), W5025/W5027 (share/dividend)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stale-content risk**: Outdated financials/disclosures on the site → misinformation/disclosure risk; mitigated by freshness governance
- **Channel-failure risk**: Disclosure not timely posted → selective-disclosure breach under RA 8799 / SEC fair-disclosure rules (W5017); mitigated by SLA & SEC-filing integration
- **Privacy/accessibility risk**: Investor-data breach or inaccessible site (RA 10173/RA 7277); mitigated by controls
System Touchpoints: - IR website/CMS; SEC-filing integration (W5018/W5019); webcast; privacy/accessibility (VS-91); records retention (VS-88); IT (VS-27)

steps.a: GM, Digital Commerce Inc. / VP IR
steps.activity: Operate the IR website/portal: the investor section (results, annual report W5018, presentations, ASHM/proxy materials W5020, share/dividend info W5025/W5027), secure analyst/investor portals, webcasts (W5011), and the disclosure archive ensuring every disclosure is publicly and simultaneously available (fair disclosure W5017)

Govern content & accessibility: accuracy/freshness of all IR content, RA 7277/BP 344 accessibility, RA 10173 data-privacy (investor contact data), records retention (VS-88), and brand standard (VS-14)

Manage digital disclosure channels & integrations: SEC/electronic filing integration (links W5018/W5019), notification/alerting to subscribers, and the audit trail of what was published when (disclosure evidence W5017)

fields.Participants: IR Analyst, CFO/CEO (escalation), Legal (VS-100), Treasury (VS-18), ESG (VS-25)
fields.Trigger: Investor/analyst inbound inquiry; proactive-outreach campaign; event follow-up
fields.Volume: ~200–400 inquiries per year × audiences + proactive outreach cadence

workflows.name: Investor Inquiry, CRM & Proactive-Outreach Response Management

Automation Opportunity: - Inquiry CRM/routing; public-info response library; sentiment capture; outreach cadence automation
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749: public-info-only responses; material inquiries escalated; fair-disclosure enforced (W5017); interactions logged
Cross-references: - links to W5010 (database), W5017 (disclosure), W5019 (rumor/ad-hoc), W5024 (feedback-to-management), W5029 (sentiment), VS-100 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Selective-disclosure risk**: Answering an inquiry with material non-public info (W5017/RA 8799); mitigated by public-info-only rule & escalation
- **Inquiry-leak risk**: Unhandled/rumored inquiry becoming market rumor (W5019); mitigated by timely fair response
- **CRM-gap risk**: Lost institutional memory of investor interactions; mitigated by CRM logging
System Touchpoints: - IR CRM (W5010); disclosure-controls (W5017); analytics (VS-28/W5029); legal (VS-100); treasury (VS-18)

steps.activity: Handle inbound investor/analyst inquiries: log in the IR CRM, route to SME (treasury/ESG/legal), respond only with public/disclosed information (fair-disclosure W5017), and escalate material/significant inquiries to CFO; never disclose material non-public info
Run proactive outreach: targeted investor/analyst meetings/calls (per W5010 targeting), relationship maintenance, and coverage development — on fair-disclosure basis with approved materials (W5017)
Capture & analyze: log every interaction in CRM (W5010), capture feedback/sentiment (W5029), and feed insights to management (W5024) and the IR plan (W5009)

fields.Participants: ESG (VS-25), CSR/Foundation (VS-152), Strategy (VS-33), Legal (VS-100), Treasury (VS-18), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Trigger: ESG-reporting cycle (VS-25); sustainable-finance/investor demand; rating/index inclusion
fields.Volume: ~10–20 ESG-investor/agency engagements per year × reporting cycles

Automation Opportunity: - ESG-data-to-investor-response mapping; rating-platform integration; greenwashing-consistency check
Controls: - CTL-749 (ensure controlled execution — Investor Relations Program, Shareholder Communications & Capital-Markets Engagement (PA-173.1).)
- CTL-749: ESG-investor claims substantiated & consistent with VS-25; fair-disclosure (W5017); greenwashing-controlled
Cross-references: - links to VS-25 (ESG), VS-152 (CSR/foundation), VS-18/VS-170 (sustainable finance), VS-22 (compliance), W5017 (disclosure), W5018 (annual report), W5029 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Greenwashing risk**: Overstated ESG claims to investors → reputational/regulatory risk (VS-25); mitigated by substantiation & consistency with filed ESG data
- **ESG-data-mismatch risk**: Investor ESG answers disagreeing with the sustainability report (VS-25); mitigated by single-source reconciliation
- **Selective-disclosure risk**: ESG material info shared selectively (W5017); mitigated by fair-disclosure
System Touchpoints: - ESG reporting (VS-25); CSR (VS-152); treasury/sustainable-finance (VS-18/VS-170); disclosure-controls (W5017); analytics (VS-28); legal (VS-100)

steps.activity: Manage ESG-investor & rating-agency engagement: respond to ESG questionnaires/ratings (MSCI/Sustainalytics-equivalent, links VS-25), ESG-investor meetings (fair-disclosure W5017), and index/inclusion programs — all reconciled to the published ESG/sustainability report (VS-25) and group annual report (W5018)

Communicate sustainable-finance & stakeholder value: green/sustainability-linked financing narrative (links VS-18/VS-170), community/foundation impact (links VS-152), and the multi-stakeholder (customer/employee/community/regulator) value story to investors

Govern ESG-investor disclosure: ensure ESG-investor claims are substantiated, consistent with filed ESG/sustainability disclosures (VS-25), free of greenwashing (links VS-22 compliance, VS-25), and disclosed fairly (W5017)
